input.strategy_title: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Data scientists iterate across dozens of training and pipeline runs but have no
way to compare them inside the platform: parameters and metrics live in
per-run pages, so comparison happens in exported spreadsheets. Model promotion
decisions need side-by-side visibility into what changed between candidate
runs and how their metrics differ. (Requirements below were consolidated from
two customer councils; some overlap in wording was kept from the sources.)

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Users can select two or more runs and view their parameters and metrics side by side in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Registered model versions link back to the run that produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | Provide a run "diff" view that highlights which parameters and metrics changed between two selected runs. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Model Registry
- Data Science Pipelines

## Out of Scope

- Automatic best-run selection or promotion
- Comparison across clusters or across projects

## Open Questions

None.

# Run comparison view for training and pipeline runs

## Description

This epic delivers a run comparison view in the Dashboard. Users can select
two or more runs from the runs list and view their parameters and metrics side
by side, and when exactly two runs are selected the comparison highlights
which parameters and metrics changed between them. The comparison works for
both training runs and Data Science Pipelines runs, so data scientists can
iterate across dozens of runs without exporting to spreadsheets.

## Scope

- Multi-run selection on the runs list (two or more runs).
- A comparison view presenting each selected run's parameters and metrics side
  by side.
- A diff presentation of the comparison for two selected runs, highlighting
  the parameters and metrics whose values differ.
- The comparison reads run parameters and metrics uniformly for training runs
  and Data Science Pipelines runs (Data Science Pipelines is a passive
  component here — no changes are expected in it; its run data is already
  surfaced through the Dashboard).
- Comparison is scoped within a single project and cluster; no automatic
  best-run selection or promotion (explicitly out of scope in the strategy).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the runs list, when a user selects two or more runs and invokes the
  comparison action, then a comparison view shows each selected run's
  parameters and metrics side by side.
- Given exactly two selected runs, the comparison highlights the parameters
  and metrics whose values differ between the two runs.
- Given a mix of training runs and Data Science Pipelines runs, the comparison
  renders parameters and metrics for both run types correctly (passive
  validation of Data Science Pipelines: no changes expected there; a failure
  means the comparison view does not surface run data uniformly).
- The comparison action and view operate only on runs within the same project
  and cluster; no cross-project or cross-cluster comparison is offered.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — users can select two or more runs and view their parameters
  and metrics side by side in the Dashboard.
- **HLR-3 (P1)** — the run "diff" view highlighting which parameters and
  metrics changed between two selected runs is a presentation mode of the same
  comparison surface and is covered by this epic; the strategy consolidates
  the two requirements (noted in the decomposition summary as a redundant/
  overlapping HLR pair, covered at the higher priority).

# Registered model version linkage to producing run

## Description

This epic delivers run lineage in the Model Registry: registered model
versions record a link back to the run that produced them, and a user can open
the run comparison from the Model Registry for a linked version. This gives
model promotion decisions side-by-side visibility into the candidate runs
behind registered versions.

## Scope

- Record a reference to the producing run on registered model versions, using
  the registry's existing extension point for structured metadata on model
  versions.
- Surface the run link on the model version through the registry's API so
  other consumers can resolve a version's producing run.
- Provide an affordance in the Model Registry view to open the run comparison
  for a version's linked run, building on the run-comparison capability in the
  Dashboard (this epic depends on that capability existing).
- Out of scope: automatic best-run selection or promotion, and comparison
  across clusters or projects.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a model version is registered in the context of a run, the version
  records a link to that producing run.
- The run link on a model version is retrievable through the registry's API.
- Given a registered model version with a run link, when a user opens the
  comparison from the Model Registry, then the run comparison loads with the
  linked run selectable alongside other runs of the same project.
- Versions registered without run context degrade gracefully (no link shown;
  no error).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-2 (P1)** — registered model versions link back to the run that
  produced them, so a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry.

# Documentation for the run comparison workflow

## Description

This epic documents the run comparison workflow end to end: how data
scientists select runs and compare parameters and metrics side by side, how
the diff view highlights what changed between two runs, and how to open a
comparison from the Model Registry via a model version's run link. The
documentation follows the Red Hat docs content process.

## Scope

Content outline:

- Selecting two or more runs from the runs list and opening the side-by-side
  comparison of parameters and metrics.
- Using the diff view to see which parameters and metrics changed between two
  selected runs.
- Opening a comparison from the Model Registry by following a registered model
  version's link to its producing run.
- Scope boundaries of the feature as documented behavior: comparison within a
  project and cluster; no automatic best-run selection or promotion.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Published documentation covers the comparison workflow starting from the
  runs list: multi-run selection, side-by-side parameters and metrics, and the
  diff view between two runs.
- Published documentation covers opening a comparison from the Model Registry
  via a registered model version's run link.
- The content is technically reviewed against the implemented behavior of both
  the Dashboard comparison and the Model Registry run linkage before
  publication.

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-4 (P2)** — documentation covers the comparison workflow from both the
  runs list and the registry. (Epic priority is P1 per the docs-authoring
  priority exception: strategy priority Major → P1.)

# Decomposition Summary — RHAISTRAT-9015: Experiment comparison for training and pipeline runs

The strategy adds run comparison to the platform: users select two or more
training or pipeline runs and view parameters and metrics side by side (with a
diff mode between two runs) in the Dashboard, registered model versions link
back to the run that produced them so a comparison can be opened from the
Model Registry, and the workflow is documented.

**Triage (Step 0):** not below-threshold and not docs-only. The strategy spans
multiple active components (Dashboard, Model Registry) and multiple distinct
work streams (Dashboard UI implementation, Model Registry metadata/linkage
work, and substantive documentation authoring per HLR-4), so the multi-epic
path applies.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9015-E001 | Run comparison view for training and pipeline runs | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9015-E002 | Registered model version linkage to producing run | Implementation | Model Registry | P1 |
| RHAISTRAT-9015-E003 | Documentation for the run comparison workflow | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHOAI Dashboard | P1 |

Notes on epic assignments:

- **Teams** derive from the architecture-context owning teams
  (`architecture/rhoai-3.0/dashboard.md` → RHOAI Dashboard,
  `architecture/rhoai-3.0/model-registry.md` → Model Registry). The strategy
  provides no Impacted Teams table (see Health Warnings).
- **E003 team** is assigned to RHOAI Dashboard (the primary documented surface)
  because the Documentation component has no owning team in the architecture
  context; confirm with docs owners before scheduling.
- **E003 priority** is P1 via the docs-authoring priority exception: the
  strategy frontmatter priority is Major → P1, overriding the P2 label on
  HLR-4 (see HLR Traceability Matrix).

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001 Run comparison view (Dashboard)"] --> E002["E002 Model version run linkage (Model Registry)"]
    E001 --> E003["E003 Comparison workflow documentation"]
    E002 --> E003
```

Critical path: E001 → E002 → E003 (length 3).

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 13 (artifact another epic builds against) | HLR-2's deliverable is not just storing a run link on a model version — it is "a comparison can be opened from the Model Registry". That entry point builds against the run-comparison surface E001 introduces; shipping it first would produce a dead affordance. The linkage storage itself is independent work inside the same epic. |
| E001 → E003 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Documentation describes the comparison workflow delivered by the Dashboard implementation; docs-authoring is blocked by every Implementation epic. |
| E002 → E003 | Rule 11 (docs last) | HLR-4 requires docs to cover the workflow "from both the runs list and the registry", so the docs must also follow the Model Registry implementation. |

No konflux-onboarding, repo-onboarding, or license-validation epics: all three
affected components exist in the architecture context and are already Konflux
onboarded, and no new component or external dependency is introduced. No
Investigation epics: the strategy states "Open Questions: None" and no
conditional ADRs, pending reviews, or risks tables are present.

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) | Analysis |
|-----|----------|---------|----------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | E001 | Direct: multi-run side-by-side comparison of parameters and metrics in the Dashboard. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | E001 | **Consolidated** with HLR-1 (redundant/overlapping HLR): the "diff view" is a presentation mode of the same comparison surface over the same run parameters and metrics — same component (Dashboard), same team, same UI surface and data. Per the redundant-HLR rule it is ONE capability covered by a single epic at the higher priority (P0); splitting would produce two epics building the same surface plus an artificial serialization edge. The P1 label reads as relative value, not a deferral signal. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | E002 | Direct: registered model versions link back to the producing run; comparison openable from the Model Registry. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | E003 | Docs-authoring epic exempt from priority inheritance; priority derived from strategy frontmatter (Major → P1). Covers the comparison workflow from both the runs list and the registry. |

All four HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Component Mapping

| Strategy component | Canonical component | Classification | Handling |
|--------------------|---------------------|----------------|----------|
| Dashboard | Dashboard | Active (code changes) | E001 |
| Model Registry | Model Registry | Active (code changes) | E002 — note: E002's scope spans onto the Dashboard surface: the "open the comparison from the Model Registry" affordance lives in the Model Registry view, which per `architecture/rhoai-3.0/model-registry.md` is surfaced through the Dashboard console ("Dashboard for the registry UI"). The Model Registry team's epic therefore touches Dashboard-rendered surface for that affordance, coordinated with the Dashboard console rather than a separate Dashboard epic (the underlying comparison capability is E001's). |
| Data Science Pipelines | Data Science Pipelines | Passive (listed as affected, no changes described; pipeline runs are already surfaced in the Dashboard per `architecture/rhoai-3.0/data-science-pipelines.md`) | Validation becomes an acceptance criterion on E001: the comparison must render parameters and metrics for Data Science Pipelines runs as well as training runs. Same platform, so no separate validation epic. |
| (docs work) | Documentation | Active (content authoring) | E003 — substantive new doc topics are a distinct work stream, not an incidental touch-up. |

All canonical names are verbatim from `.context/rhai-components.txt`; no
non-obvious mappings were needed.

## Health Warnings

1. **Missing refinement sections** (non-blocking): the strategy has no
   Impacted Teams table, no Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then acceptance
   criteria, no NFRs, and the Affected Components section is a bare list
   without per-component change/owner detail. Team assignments were derived
   from architecture-context owning teams; ACs were derived from HLRs.
2. **Docs epic team assumption**: E003 is assigned to RHOAI Dashboard by
   default (primary documented surface); the Documentation component has no
   owning team recorded in the architecture context.
3. **Docs priority vs HLR label**: HLR-4 is labeled P2 while E003 is P1 —
   intentional, per the docs-authoring priority exception (strategy priority
   Major → P1).
4. **Passive-component assumption**: Data Science Pipelines is treated as
   passive — the Dashboard already surfaces pipeline runs (KFP v2 API per
   `data-science-pipelines.md`), so comparison of pipeline-run parameters and
   metrics is expected to need no DSP-side changes. If E001's validation AC
   fails (pipeline run metadata not accessible in a comparable shape), a
   follow-up Data Science Pipelines epic is required — this is an
   implementation-detail risk, not a genuine unknown (the strategy flags no
   open questions).
5. **Priority inversions**: none detected — HLR priorities are consistent with
   the technical scope.
6. **Parallel-start eligibility of E002's metadata work**: the E001 → E002 edge
   (Rule 13) exists for the registry entry point that builds against the
   run-comparison surface; it also serializes E002's linkage-storage work
   (recording and exposing the run link on model versions), which is
   independent of E001. If capacity demands, that metadata work can start in
   parallel with E001 — only the entry-point affordance needs to wait for the
   comparison capability.

No epic exceeds ~2 weeks of estimated effort; no re-split triggers recorded.

## Tiered Delivery

Not applicable — no external dependencies with uncertain timing; all work is
in-platform across components already at GA maturity.
